_comment: What a package still cannot bring in its own folder (src/portability.py serves this to Dev Lab ▸ Model Interactions). Each anchor is `path::text` and must still be in that file while the gap is open; test_portability.py fails when one is gone, so closing a gap means changing its status here in the same change. kind: gate | tooling | commons | code | client | watch | docs. impact on a dropped-in package: blocks (it fails a gate or cannot be written), degrades (it works, worse or silently wrong), cosmetic. status: open | by_design (the commons vocabulary is the contract between packages and the engine). roadmap: the step of docs/roadmap.md item 9 (9.1, 9.2, …) that closes it.
verdict: The code is package-neutral: nothing in the server, the web, the phones or the watches names a package (tools/check_code_neutral.py), and test_package_dropin.py runs three packages under new ids beside the shipped ones with the repository unchanged. A new folder is brought in with one command (tools/add_package.py <id>), which writes the records the push gates keep outside it; a package may bring its own standards (standards.yaml); anything else beyond the commons vocabulary is still a shared edit.

gaps.title: A package's records live outside its folder: the scorecard and coverage baselines, status.yaml, the golden program hashes and the dossier
gaps.detail: One command writes them for that package only (tools/add_package.py <id>), refusing a fidelity finding, an orphaned exercise, an id another package declares or one the commons lack; until it runs, the push gates fail on the new package. They could live in the folder itself.

gaps.title: A package's own tests count only once listed in the shared suite registry
gaps.detail: A fidelity rule enforced_by a test is debt (S3) until checks/python_suites.yaml lists the test, and tools/run_checks.py refuses an unlisted root test.

gaps.title: Blends are checked on five fixed pairs
gaps.detail: A new package's tracks are generated on their own; it is never generated in a blend.

gaps.title: What each watch template records is not declared
gaps.detail: X2 checks every step has a screen, not that the package's lead measure is captured on the wrist.

gaps.title: The MCP server's schema list is stale and it ignores TRAINING_PACKAGES_DIR
gaps.detail: It names goal_profile.schema.json, which does not exist, and writes analytics, watch, contract, fidelity and source-week files unvalidated.

gaps.title: The extraction guide puts standards and data outside the package
The author guide's schema sections predate tracks, week templates and contracts
gaps.detail: Sections 5–13 still teach framework_groups, goals_served and goal profiles; the schemas in docs/schemas/ are the reference.

gaps.title: Phase kinds, intensities, levels and progression and contract models are engine vocabulary
gaps.detail: A package chooses among them; a new one is engine work.

gaps.title: Scheduling and load constants are code
gaps.detail: Recovery-cost ranks, the 48 h floor between two high-cost modalities, RPE load factors and the progression defaults (2.5 kg increment, 3 × 5, two sessions a week) are the engine's, the same for every package.
